1. This is a revision petition filed by the revisionist under section 397/399 Cr.PC. for setting-aside the impugned order dated 02.09.2023 (hereinafter referred to as impugned order) passed by the Court of Ld. MM/North (Mahila Court-02), North- District, Rohini Courts, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as Ld. Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr.
Trial Court) in Cr Case No. 1243/2021, titled as 'State Vs. Aman Sood' whereby the charge for the offences punishable U/s 406 IPC was framed against the revisionist / accused Usha Rani Sood.
2. Being aggrieved by the impugned order, the Revisionist has moved the present revision petition on the following grounds :
(i) Because the impugned order dated 02.09.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court is illegal,
arbitrary, improper and unsustainable under law.

(ii) Because the Ld. Trial Court has passed the impugned order without consideration that complainant had opted to lodge her completely false and frivolous complaint and FIR after a gap of 21 years from the alleged date of occurrence and as section 406 IPC Usha Rani Sood vs State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40798784/
1 has provision of maximum punishment upto three years only, hence, in every eventuality the limitation period for the said section shall be three years only.

sentences.text: As the complainant had opted to lodge her complaint after a gap of 21 years, hence, it got hit by section 468 Cr. PC and is barred by limitation.

(iii) That the complainant nowhere mentioned the exact date and time when she demanded back her stridhan and as she had live separately for 18 years and at the time of leaving the house of revisionist voluntarily, the complainant had taken all her Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr.
ornaments and stridhan with her and hence, in those 18 years, she had no occasion or reason to demand back her stridhan.

sentences.text: When in 2015, the complainant had cajoled and persuaded the revisionist to construct another floor and in that newly added floor, the complainant along with her husband and children got license to re-enter then again it was a separate accommodation altogether having separate entry and exit and hence again there was no reason or occasion for any eventuality of section 406 IPC.

(iv) That the complainant had alleged offences under section 498A by revisionist and her family but she had voluntarily opted to re-enter the same house after staying separately for more than 18 years and it raises doubt in prudent mind because any prudent person would not go to stay in the same place where he / she had been harassed in any manner in the past.

(v) That the Ld. Trial Court had dropped charges under section 498A IPC against the revisionist on the ground that the alleged allegation of complainant does not suffice the four corners of said sections.
In matrimonial dispute section 406 IPC cannot stand alone in solitary because without any sort of cruelty or use of force any person cannot be compelled to part away with his / her belongings.

Once the allegation under Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr.
section 498A IPC could not pass the test on judicial touchstone then under section 406A IPC would also dash to the ground.

The complainant has not bothered to file any list pertaining to her stridhan and it has also causes doubt on the mind that her allegation is very general in nature and has been alleged with sole intention to falsely implicate and blackmail the complainant and her family.

(vii) Because the Ld. Trial Court has not appreciated and considered the fact that revisionist has filed the list of complaint qua torture and blackmailing done by complainant well before the FIR in question was lodged by the complainant and it gives a simple impression of counter-blast against complaints lodged by revisionist and her late husband.
(viii) Because the Ld. Trial Court has grossly erred in not dropping the charge under section 406 IPC against the revisionist.

sentences.text: It is argued by Ld. Counsel for Revisionist that there is no mention of any incident or ingredient which could amount to offence punishable under Section 406 IPC against revisionist / accused Usha Rani Sood and not a single word was whispered about any of the incident to fulfill the criteria of Section 406 IPC.

It is prayed that revision petition filed by revisionist may kindly be allowed and revisionist / accused Dr. Usha Rani Sood may kindly be discharged from the charge for the offence punishable U/s 406 IPC.
4.

On the other hand, Ld. APP for State / Respondent has opposed the contentions made by Ld.
Counsel for revisionist / accused and submits that there is enough material available on record,
which enables the Court to frame charge.
Ld. APP for State / Respondent has vehemently opposed the present revision petition and prayed that the present revision petition may kindly be dismissed.
He has further argued that revision petition is not maintainable as charge has been framed only on the basis of material available on record.
5. I have given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of ld.
Counsel for the revisionist/accused as well as Ld. APP for State / Respondent.
This Court has also perused the record.

Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, Trial Court Record has been summoned and the same has been carefully perused.

Perusal of the Trial Court Record shows that the FIR in the instant case was registered on the basis of the hand written complaint of the Complainant dated 30.08.2017 wherein the complainant has leveled specific allegations against revisionist / accused Usha Rani Sood that on the very next day of her marriage, her mother-in-law i.e., revisionist had taken all her jewelery articles which were given to her at the time of her marriage by her parents on the pretext that she (revisionist) would keep the same in her custody.

Further, complainant has leveled a specific allegations against her mother-in-law that she (revisionist) had given one of her gold necklace and two gold bangles to her sister-in-law Sonia and Sharda without her consent.
Thus, there are specific allegations of committing the offence of criminal breach of trust punishable under section 406 IPC against the revisionist.
7. Ld.

Counsel for revisionist has argued that Ld. Trial Court has passed impugned order without consideration that complainant had not registered the present FIR after gap of twenty one years from the date of occurrence and the section 406 IPC provides for maximum punishment upto three years only, therefore, in every eventuality, the limitation for the period for the said section shall be three years only, therefore, cognizance of the afore-said offence is barred by limitation.

sentences.text:
The term 'Criminal Breach of Trust' has been defined in section 405 IPC, 1860 which reads as follows:-
"Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes off that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract,
express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do,
commits "criminal breach of trust".

9. In case titled as 'Balram Singh v. Sukhwant Kaur & Anr.' Criminal Misc. No.7923-M of 1989, it has been held that "having regard to the nature of offence and the purpose which is intended to be achieved while constituting criminal breach of trust as on offence, we are of the view that the offence in question is a continuing one".
10.

entities.text: Balram Singh v. Sukhwant Kaur & Anr.' Criminal Misc. No.7923-M of 1989
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From bare perusal of the definition of the term "Criminal Breach of Trust" as defined in IPC as well as in the light of the afore- mentioned case law, it can be concluded that the offence punishable under section 406 IPC is a continuing offence till the property in question is restored to the person entitled to its possession.

In the present case, specific allegations of Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr.
committing the offence punishable under section 406 IPC has been leveled and as per the complaint, stridhan articles were never returned to the complainant, therefore, the offence alleged against revisionist continues and the said offence is not hit by bar of limitation as prescribed in section 468 IPC.

entities.text: Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, this contention of Ld. Counsel for revisionist is not maintainable and is liable to be rejected.
11. It is important to mention that at the stage of framing of charge, Court has to see whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
It is axiomatic that even the strong suspicion that the accused has committed the crime, is sufficient to frame the charges.
It is also well settled that the standard of proof adhered to at the final decision of the case is not to be adopted at the stage of framing of charge.
The Court is not to appreciate or weigh the evidence, which the prosecution proposes to lead during the trial.
Even, otherwise, the veracity of the complainant can only be ascertained after recording her evidence in the Court.

In the present case, from perusal of the Trial Court Record, this Court is of view that Ld. Trial Court has rightly framed charge against present revionist as the record available before Ld. Trial Court was sufficient to make an opinion that prima facie charge for the offence punishable under section 406 IPC was made against present revisionist Ms. Usha Rani Sood.

Usha Rani Sood Vs State & Anr.
12.

sentences.text: In view of the above discusssion, this Court is of view that there is no illegality, infirmity or perversity in the impugned order dated 02.09.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court.
Same is accordingly upheld and the present revision petition is hereby dismissed.
